name: Cloudflare
summary: Cloudflare's careers page describes a recruiter conversation about your background and the role, a panel with your prospective manager and peers focused on how you think and solve problems, and calls with leaders about vision and values that include what it calls the Orange Cloud Interview. Cloudflare has written that final-stage candidates meet an executive leader, and engineering hires commonly report several interviews plus a pair programming exercise.
rounds: Recruiter conversation about your background and the role
Team panel with your prospective manager and peers: problem-solving and how you think
Technical interviews and often a pair programming exercise (engineering)
Calls with leaders about vision and values, including the Orange Cloud Interview
looks_for: Care for building a better Internet

questions.text: Tell me about a hard technical problem you solved. How did you approach it?
covers: How you broke it down and what you tried
The solution and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you learned something new quickly to get a job done.
covers: What you needed to learn and why

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with another team to fix a problem neither owned alone.
covers: The problem and who was involved

questions.text: Tell me about an incident or outage you were part of. What did you do?
What happens, step by step, when someone types a website address into a browser?
covers: The request, the response and where a CDN fits in

questions.text: How would you protect a website from a sudden flood of traffic meant to take it down?
covers: Telling real users from attack traffic
Rate limits, challenges and spreading load

questions.text: How would you design a cache that serves content from data centres around the world?
covers: What to cache and for how long

questions.text: How would you explain how encryption keeps web traffic private to a non-technical friend?
Let's pair: write a small rate limiter that allows a set number of requests per minute per user.
covers: Choosing an approach: fixed window, sliding window or token bucket
How it would work across many servers

questions.text: How would you decide what to log and monitor for a new service?
covers: Signals that show users are affected
Alerts that are worth waking someone for

questions.text: Why do you want to work at Cloudflare?
covers: What draws you to Cloudflare's mission or products
How your skills fit the role

questions.text: What would you want to ask Cloudflare's leaders about the company's direction?
covers: A question about where the product is going
A question about the team's challenges
Something you read from Cloudflare's blog

tips: Read a few recent posts on Cloudflare's blog: they show how the company thinks and explains technology.
In the panel, think out loud; Cloudflare says it focuses on how you think and solve problems.
Be ready to talk about values and vision with a leader in the final calls.
Revise networking basics such as DNS, TLS and HTTP if you're applying for a technical role.

sources.title: Cloudflare blog: Helping to build Cloudflare, part 5 (people and hiring)
